header:
Date: 2027-10-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Saddleback Head of ML), Liam O'Neill (Saddleback Platform), Sofia Ruiz (Saddleback CTO)
summary: POC scoping to validate reserved GPU baseline + burst strategy for Saddleback's inference workloads. Agreed POC success criteria: 1) sustained 1200 QPS for 95th percentile within 100ms tail on a representative subset; 2) cost per 1M tokens under target budget agreed in SOW; 3) safe fallback to cheaper model variant with <2% error delta; 4) telemetry and audit logs visible in console. Next: Redwood to supply reserved GPU sizing options, benchmark plan, and fallback policy draft; customer to provide traces and SLOs. Timeline: lab kickoff week of 2027-11-01, 3-week run, decision by 2027-11-29.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about an hour, we'll focus on the capacity scoping and the burst/fallback plan for the poc. quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya (Saddleback): hi all, maya here, thanks.
[00:15] Liam (Saddleback): liam here.
[00:17] Sofia (Saddleback): sofia joining.
[00:20] Priya (SE): priya from redwood, hi. ethan on as well.
[00:24] Ethan: hey.
[00:30] Jordan: cool. to set expectations, this call is to lock down success criteria, sizing for reserved gpus, burst policy and fallback. we want to avoid the usual back-and-forth where reserved is undersized and the app hits timeouts.
[00:45] Maya: yeah we're trying to get a predictable baseline for our real-time chat assistant, at peak we saw spikes up to about 1.6k qps but average sits around 400 qps. for poc we can limit to a subset of traffic.
[00:58] Priya: helpful — can you confirm p50/p95 tails you care about?
[01:02] Maya: p50 we're fine with 40-60ms, p95 ideally under 120ms, p99 under 350 but that's less critical.
[01:12] Jordan: great. so for the poc we'll aim to demonstrate 95th percentile under 100-120ms to be safe. cost target?
[01:20] Sofia: finance wants an estimate — ballpark under $120 per 1M tokens processed at the poc scale.
[01:27] Ethan: okay noted. a few clarifying Qs: what's your median sequence length and the model family you plan to use?
[01:34] Maya: median ~80 tokens, 99th about 600. model — we're evaluating openLM-style medium chat models right now, nothing huge like 70b but similar architecture.
[01:45] Priya: that guides quantization and kernel choices — good. for reserved sizing we usually map based on baseline steady qps and burst headroom. if you want to simulate 1200 sustained for the test we'll recommend a 2-node reserved pool of A100-ish equivalents with burst pool on demand.
[02:02] Liam: are you saying reserved plus on-demand burst? we have procurement limits on how many on-demand nodes we can spin.
[02:09] Jordan: yes, reserved pool for predictable throughput + a burst tier that can be short-lived. we can configure burst caps and preemptive queueing so that requests don't time out. important detail: burst capacity is not unlimited and we'll fall back to lower-cost variants or request queuing based on policy.
[02:26] Maya: okay what's the expected cost difference if we use bursts heavily?
[02:30] Ethan: bursts at on-demand prices can double effective unit cost if used continuously, which is why the fallback is critical — you'd route excess to a quantized 4-bit variant or to a lower latency cheaper model.
[02:42] Jordan: and for the poc we can show both strategies: burst + queueing and burst + fallback. We'll run benchmark permutations.
[02:50] [02:50] Sofia: pause — can you explain the fallback in practice? is it auto or manual?
[02:55] Priya: good q. we can implement automatic fallback rules: e.g., when reserved utilization > 85% for 30s, route new requests to fallback model A (4-bit quantized) up to 30% of traffic, or enqueue requests for up to 5s before failing over. rules are policy-driven and you can tune thresholds.
[03:16] Liam: what about correctness — we can't have hallucination increase.
[03:20] Priya: right — during the poc we'll run a small evaluator harness with metric buckets — bleu/ROUGE isn't perfect for chat but we'll use human-sampled evals and a drift monitor. acceptance criteria: fallback must keep error delta < 2% on our key prompt set.
[03:36] Maya: meaningful — we'll provide a test corpus of 1,200 prompts, and a 200-sample human review set.
[03:44] Jordan: perfect. about autoscaling: Redwood's Dedicated pool supports target-based autoscale plus time-window predictions. for poc we'll set a conservative policy: scale-up on sustained queue depth > 40 and scale-down after 60s stable.
[03:57] Ethan: quick note — autoscaling granularity is at the node level and we bias toward cold-start-resilient kernels to avoid 2-3s spinup latency. but burst nodes are warm if we pre-warm VM images.
[04:08] Sofia: pre-warming sounds essential. how much lead time?
[04:12] Priya: with pre-warm we can get <15s warmup for a small node image; without pre-warm cold start could be 45-90s depending on infra.
[04:21] Liam: procurement again — pre-warm may require reserved credit or warm pool charges.
[04:25] Jordan: we can include warm pool cost in the poc estimate.
[04:29] [04:29] Maya: benchmarks — what will you run?
[04:32] Priya: plan: (1) steady-state throughput test at 400 qps for baseline; (2) sustained 1200 qps validation run for 10 minutes; (3) spike series with 0->1600 qps ramps to test burst; (4) fallback correctness runs using sample corpus. we'll collect latency percentiles, token cost, model delta, KV cache hit rates.
[04:54] Jordan: please add memory pressure tests for longer sequences — 600-token tails.
[04:58] Priya: will add. also we capture trace logs for every request and send them to your SIEM via S3 or streaming.
[05:05] Liam: on security — we need SOC2 attestation, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. what's supported?
[05:12] Ethan: Redwood Private supports customer KMS + HSM integration, audit logs retained in console; hosted has SOC2 Type II but for per-tenant KMS you need Private or Dedicated with KMS passthrough.
[05:24] Sofia: we'd prefer Private but procurement sees higher friction; for the poc Dedicated with encryption at rest and SSO might suffice.
[05:32] Jordan: noted — we'll include a comparison matrix in the docs.
[05:36] Maya: timeline — we're targeting a decision before the end of november; engineering bandwidth is limited the second half of nov due to a product launch.
[05:44] Jordan: so lab kickoff week of 2027-11-01 works?
[05:47] Maya: yes that works if we get the benchmark template and SOW this week.
[05:53] Priya: action items: we'll draft fallback policy variants (queue-first, fallback-first, hybrid) and send.
[05:59] Liam: for the fallback-first variant what's the typical user-visible latency?
[06:03] Priya: fallback-first can keep median similar, but p95 will shift depending on variant. in our experience median changes <10ms but p95 may move 30-90ms depending on model gap.
[06:14] [06:14] Maya: that might be acceptable, we care about overall user experience more than strict p50.
[06:20] Jordan: ok, on measurement — we'll expose a telemetry dashboard with per-route token costs and a rollback button for any rollout.
[06:28] Ethan: also adding canary routing: roll out new reserved-sizing or higher concurrency nodes to 5% of traffic, evaluate perf for 24h, then increase.
[06:38] Sofia: good — procurement will like the rollback safety.
[06:42] Maya: are we able to run synthetic traffic from our region to simulate real network hops?
[06:46] Priya: yes we support region-based generator nodes; please tell us which cloud region you want tests from.
[06:52] Liam: likely us-west-2.
[06:55] Jordan: we'll set that up.
[06:58] [06:58] Maya: question on logging PII — some of our traces include user names, can we redact?
[07:03] Ethan: yes we support field-level redaction before shipping to our storage endpoints; for Private you can self-host logs.
[07:10] Priya: small operational note — if your workload uses long-lived KV caches we recommend pinning certain models to the same pool to avoid cache misses during fallback.
[07:20] Liam: how do you do pinning?
[07:22] Priya: routing policy can bind a user cohort to a pool name or node label, that keeps KV locality.
[07:28] Maya: that's ideal for our sessioned conversations.
[07:31] Jordan: onto acceptance tests: list I'll read — 1) pass 1200 sustained qps 95th <120ms on representative shard; 2) fallback path error delta <2% on sampled prompts; 3) cost per M tokens < $120; 4) logs and SSO accessible; 5) demo of autoscale behavior under spike. agree?
[07:48] Sofia: agree.
[07:50] Maya: agree.
[07:51] Jordan: good. scheduling — we'll aim to run the benchmark matrix across 3 calendar weeks: prep week (instrumentation + sample traces), execution week (bench runs), review/fine-tune week. final decision by 2027-11-29.
[08:08] Liam: if we bump into procurement delays, can we run a reduced-scope lab on hosted?
[08:12] Jordan: yes, hosted can demo similar behavior but without per-tenant KMS and reserved pool guarantees. it's good for early validation.
[08:20] Maya: competitors — LargeCloudX pushed us a proposal that uses autoscale nodes only — cost looks lower on paper but no fallback model.
[08:28] Jordan: we've seen that trade-off — lower headline cost, but risk of higher tail latency and no graceful degrade.
[08:33] [08:33] Ethan: technical deep dive we might run during the lab: kernel selection and sequence memory pressure; we can include that as an optional session.
[08:42] Priya: I'll prepare the benchmark harness and share a sample Jenkins/runner job so you can re-run locally.
[08:49] Jordan: let's recap next steps, I'll list them: 1) Jordan to send SOW + pricing + reserved options by 2027-10-28. 2) Priya to send benchmark template + fallback policy variants by 2027-10-27. 3) Maya to provide sample corpus and peak QPS traces by 2027-10-28. 4) Liam to share network/VPC constraints by 2027-10-29. 5) Schedule kickoff week of 2027-11-01.
[09:16] Maya: sounds good.
[09:18] Jordan: any final questions?
[09:20] Sofia: one — after poc, if we want dedicated private we'll need a compliance pack; can you pre-check that?
[09:26] Ethan: yes we'll include compliance checklist and lead times.
[09:30] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
[09:33] Maya: thanks.
[09:35] [09:35] End of recording

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., 'kernel' sometimes transcribed as 'colonel'), minor speaker mislabels possible.
